subject: mass-communication
title: Model Question Paper 1
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 80 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
For the Optional Modules, attempt Module A (Traditional Media) or Module B (Photojournalism) in the sections that have both.

MCQs carry 1 mark; objective questions carry 2 marks (two parts of 1 mark each); very short answers carry 2 marks (30–50 words); short answers 3 marks (50–80 words); the long answer 4 marks (80–120 words).
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: Name the types of news by area.
questions.answer: International, national, regional and local news.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Name the three functions of mass media with one example each.
questions.answer: Inform – news bulletin; educate – a doctor's talk on preventing disease; entertain – films and serials.

questions.q: Differentiate between circulation and readership.
questions.answer: Circulation is the number of copies sold; readership is the number of people who read them, which is higher since one copy has many readers.

questions.q: What is a vox pop?
questions.answer: A Latin phrase meaning 'voice of people': one or two questions are put to ordinary people to measure public opinion on a current topic.

questions.q: What is the role of a floor manager?
questions.answer: He is in charge of all activities on the studio floor, conveys the director's instructions and supervises floor personnel.

questions.q: Explain any two functions of a website.
questions.answer: It gives initial information to customers and employees through a 'contact us' section, allows feedback through blogs, and offers online services such as shopping and news.

sections.title: Optional Module A (Traditional Media): attempt A or Module B. Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: List any two disadvantages of electronic media.
questions.answer: They are expensive and less intimate; feedback is slow; special training is required.

questions.q: Write a short note on any one: (i) Demonstrations (ii) Puppetry.
questions.answer: Demonstrations help transfer knowledge and encourage farmers to try new ideas, with story telling and plays at weekly markets. Puppetry combines entertainment with education and treats sensitive topics such as HIV/AIDS.

sections.title: Optional Module B (Photojournalism): attempt B or Module A. Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Name any two types of photojournalism.
questions.answer: Sports photojournalism and war photojournalism (also glamour, spot news, travel, wildlife).

questions.q: Why is 'manipulation' considered unethical in photojournalism?
questions.answer: Because the photojournalist must capture the truth; manipulating or staging an image is like making up a news story.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: List any three positive and any three negative effects of media.
questions.answer: Positive: informs and educates, helps democracy, promotes trade. Negative: harms traditional culture, promotes violence, creates desire for non-essential products.

questions.q: Explain the job of a sub-editor in editing a copy.
questions.answer: Correct language and facts, add background, write a crisp heading, add photographs or graphs, condense to fit space and suggest a byline.

questions.q: Describe the roles of the studio, control room and transmitter.
questions.answer: Studio: sound-proof room where programmes are produced; control room: technical area that sends the programmes to the transmitter; transmitter: sends waves to the listener's radio set.

questions.q: List three milestones in the history of television in India.
questions.answer: 1959 experimental start; 1975–76 SITE; 1982 national colour coverage by INSAT 1A (also 1976 Doordarshan separated, 1997 Prasar Bharati).

questions.q: Describe any three guidelines governing advertising.
questions.answer: No exaggerated or misleading claims; no direct endorsement of tobacco or liquor; no portrayal of women as passive or submissive.

questions.q: Is new media a big industry or an SME? Give reasons.
questions.answer: It is an SME as it needs little infrastructure and money but much creativity; niche websites started in small rooms and grew.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the types of public relations.
questions.answer: Product PR, employee relations, government and political relations and community relations, each with its methods.

sections.title: Optional Module A (Traditional Media): attempt A or Module B. Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Discuss the relevance of traditional media in modern society.
questions.answer: They reach rural and tribal people and illiterates, are flexible and cheap, preserve culture, give deeper impact through audience participation and are being integrated with electronic media for development messages.

sections.title: Optional Module B (Photojournalism): attempt B or Module A. Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the role played by famous photojournalists in India before and after Independence.
questions.answer: Raja Deen Dayal, Sunil Janah and Homai Vyarawalla recorded British India, partition and the freedom movement; Henri Cartier-Bresson, Raghu Rai and Prashant Panjiar documented events and leaders after independence.
